title: Delhi-Alwar RRTS Guide 2026: Route, Stations, Timeline, Fare and Everything You Need to Know
description: Complete Delhi-Alwar RRTS guide: full route map, all stations, construction timeline, expected speed, fare and everything known about this Namo Bharat corridor so far.
body:
The Delhi-Alwar RRTS, also called the Delhi-Gurugram-SNB-Alwar corridor, is one of the three Namo Bharat corridors approved under Phase 1 of India's Regional Rapid Transit System project. Once complete, it will connect Delhi with Gurugram, Rewari, and Alwar in Rajasthan, cutting a journey that currently takes three to four hours by road down to under two hours by rail.

This corridor is still under construction and has not opened to the public yet. But since so many commuters, homebuyers, and daily travellers are searching for updates on it, this guide brings together everything currently known: the full route, every planned station, the construction timeline, expected speed and travel time, and what is and isn't known yet about fares.

## Quick Facts About Delhi-Alwar RRTS

| Detail | Information |
| Full name | Delhi-Gurugram-SNB-Alwar Regional Rapid Transit System |
| Also called | Delhi-Alwar RRTS, Delhi-SNB-Alwar corridor |
| Total length | Approximately 164 km |
| States covered | Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan |
| Cities connected | Delhi, Gurugram, Manesar, Dharuhera, Rewari, Bawal, Shahjahanpur-Neemrana-Behror (SNB), Khairthal, Alwar |
| Maximum speed | Up to 160 km/h |
| Average speed | Approximately 105 km/h |
| Estimated end-to-end travel time | Around 100 to 105 minutes, Delhi to Alwar |
| Current status | Pre-construction complete, construction expected to begin around August 2026 |
| Operator | NCRTC (National Capital Region Transport Corporation) |
| Depots | Dharuhera (182 acres, main depot), Alwar (planned for later phase) |

## What Is Delhi-Alwar RRTS?

Delhi-Alwar RRTS is a planned high-speed regional rail corridor that will link Delhi to the industrial belt running through Gurugram, Rewari, and further down into Rajasthan, ending at Alwar. It is one of the three priority corridors under Phase 1 of India's Namo Bharat project, alongside the already operational Delhi-Meerut corridor and the under-construction Delhi-Panipat corridor.

Like the Delhi-Meerut line, this corridor is designed for intercity travel with widely spaced stations and trains capable of running at up to 160 km/h, which is very different from a city metro that stops every one to two kilometres. If you want to understand this distinction in more depth, our guide on the difference between [metro and RRTS](https://metroguideindia.com/blog/difference-between-metro-and-rrts-complete-comparison-2026.html) breaks down exactly how these systems differ in speed, coach design, and purpose.

## Delhi-Alwar RRTS Route: Full Corridor Breakdown

The corridor originates at **Sarai Kale Khan** in Delhi, the same station where the [Delhi-Meerut](https://metroguideindia.com/blog/begumpul-to-delhi-in-55-minutes-a-first-timer-s-complete-guide-to-the-rrts-corridor.html) and Delhi-Panipat corridors also converge, allowing commuters to switch between all three [Namo Bharat](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/) lines without leaving the station.

From Sarai Kale Khan, the route runs through:

1. **Delhi section** — [Sarai Kale Khan](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/stations/sarai-kale-khan.html), Jor Bagh (INA), Munirka, Aerocity
2. **Gurugram section** — Udyog Vihar, Gurugram Sector 17, Rajiv Chowk, Kherki Daula, Manesar, Panchgaon
3. **Rewari section** — Bilaspur Chowk, Dharuhera (main depot location), MBIR, Rewari, Bawal
4. **Rajasthan section** — Shahjahanpur-Neemrana-Behror (SNB), Khairthal, Alwar

A short spur line will also serve Shahjahanpur, Neemrana, Behror, and Sotanala, branching off the main corridor to cover this industrial stretch of Rajasthan separately.

The very first section to open, once construction is complete, is expected to be the **Delhi to Dharuhera stretch**, covering roughly 70 km with around 13 stations, similar to how the Delhi-Meerut corridor opened in phases before the full line became operational.

## Delhi-Alwar RRTS Route Map: How to Read It

The Delhi-Alwar route map runs largely along the existing Delhi-Jaipur corridor, roughly following NH-48. Delhi and Gurugram stations sit close together at the start of the line, since this is the densest, most built-up stretch. Beyond Manesar, station spacing widens considerably as the corridor moves through Rewari district and into Rajasthan, reflecting lower population density and the more industrial character of that stretch.

The **Dharuhera** stretch is particularly important on the map, since this is where the corridor's main 182-acre maintenance depot is being built, making Dharuhera a key operational hub for the entire line, similar to how Duhai Depot functions for the Delhi-Meerut corridor.

## Construction Timeline and Current Status

As of mid-2026, the Delhi-Alwar RRTS is in an advanced pre-construction stage:

- **2018** — Detailed Project Report for the Delhi-SNB corridor approved by the Government of Haryana
- **2022 to 2023** — Pre-construction work, including surveys and soil testing, carried out in the Gurugram stretch
- **October 2024** — Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs announced that commissioning of the Delhi-Panipat and Delhi-SNB-Alwar networks was expected to begin in 2025
- **November 2024** — Decision taken to develop the entire corridor in a single phase rather than splitting it into three separate construction phases
- **Late 2025** — Tender floated to appoint a General Consultant for the project, with strong industry participation reported at the pre-bid meeting
- **August 2026** — Construction is expected to begin, based on the most recent reporting available

Some real estate industry sources have projected a commercial launch around 2031 for the initial Sarai Kale Khan to Bawal stretch, with the full extension to Alwar potentially following a few years later. It is worth being cautious with any specific completion year this far out, since RRTS project timelines in India have shifted before, including on the Delhi-Meerut corridor itself. The safest way to think about it is that construction is on the verge of starting in 2026, with full commercial operations realistically several years away.

## Expected Speed and Travel Time

Once operational, Delhi-Alwar RRTS trains are expected to run at a maximum speed of up to 160 km/h, with an average speed of around 105 km/h across the full corridor, which is a higher average than the Delhi-Meerut corridor due to longer gaps between stations in the Rajasthan stretch. At these speeds, the full Delhi to Alwar journey is expected to take approximately 100 to 105 minutes, compared to the three to four hours it currently takes by road.

Shorter trips, such as Delhi to Gurugram or Delhi to Dharuhera, are expected to take considerably less time given the shorter distance covered.

## Delhi-Alwar RRTS Fare: What Is Known So Far

NCRTC has not yet announced an official fare structure for this corridor, since it is still under construction. Based on how the Delhi-Meerut corridor was priced, fares are expected to be distance based, likely following a similar Standard and Premium coach structure. Reports also mention that Delhi-Alwar trains may include a dedicated business class coach with lounge access at select stations, which would be a step beyond what the Delhi-Meerut corridor currently offers.

Once fares are officially announced, this section will be updated with the confirmed pricing structure. For now, our complete [Namo Bharat RRTS Guide](https://metroguideindia.com/blog/namo-bharat-rrts-guide-2026-routes-stations-timings-fare-complete-travel-guide.html) covers the confirmed, currently operational fare details for the Delhi-Meerut corridor, which gives a reasonable sense of how RRTS pricing generally works.

## How Delhi-Alwar RRTS Connects to the Rest of the Namo Bharat Network

All three Phase 1 Namo Bharat corridors, Delhi-Meerut, Delhi-Panipat, and Delhi-Alwar, converge at **Sarai Kale Khan** station in Delhi. This is intentional, and it means a commuter will eventually be able to travel from Meerut to Alwar, or from Panipat to Gurugram, by changing trains at a single station rather than needing to exit and re-enter the network.

Within Delhi, several stations on this corridor are also positioned near existing Delhi Metro connections, including Aerocity, which sits close to Delhi Airport and the Airport Express Line, making this corridor particularly useful for airport-bound and business travel once operational.

## Why This Corridor Matters

The Delhi-Gurugram-Rewari-Alwar stretch is one of the most industrially active corridors in North India, home to major manufacturing hubs in Manesar, Bawal, and Neemrana. A high-speed rail link here is expected to meaningfully cut commute times for factory workers, corporate employees, and businesses that currently depend entirely on road transport along NH-48, which sees heavy traffic congestion, particularly around Gurugram and Manesar.

It is also expected to have a noticeable impact on real estate demand near planned stations, similar to the property appreciation already seen near Delhi-Meerut RRTS stations after that corridor opened.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is Delhi-Alwar RRTS operational yet?

No. As of mid-2026, the corridor is in advanced pre-construction stage, with actual construction expected to begin around August 2026. It is not open to the public yet.

### How long is the Delhi-Alwar RRTS corridor?

The full corridor is approximately 164 km long, connecting Delhi to Alwar via Gurugram, Rewari, and the Shahjahanpur-Neemrana-Behror belt.

### What stations will Delhi-Alwar RRTS have?

The main line includes 18 stations from Sarai Kale Khan to Alwar, with an additional 4 stations on a spur line covering Shahjahanpur, Neemrana, Behror, and Sotanala.

### How long will it take to travel from Delhi to Alwar?

Once fully operational, the journey is expected to take approximately 100 to 105 minutes at an average speed of around 105 km/h, compared to three to four hours by road today.

### When will Delhi-Alwar RRTS be completed?

An exact completion date has not been officially confirmed. Some reports suggest the first stretch, from Sarai Kale Khan to Bawal, may become operational around 2031, with the full line to Alwar following later. These timelines can shift as construction progresses.

### What will the fare be on Delhi-Alwar RRTS?

Fares have not been officially announced yet. They are expected to follow a distance based structure similar to the Delhi-Meerut corridor, with a Standard coach and a Premium or business class option.

### Where does Delhi-Alwar RRTS start from?

The corridor starts at Sarai Kale Khan station in Delhi, the same station where the Delhi-Meerut and Delhi-Panipat Namo Bharat corridors also originate.
